item.title: 🇷🇺 On September 24, Russia’s Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov and UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres
item.description: 🇷🇺 🇺🇳 On September 24, Russia’s Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov and UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres held a meeting in New York on the sidelines of the High-Level Week of the 81st Session of the UN General Assembly . The Sides discussed current issues relating to the Organisation’s work, focusing on the record of the Portuguese diplomat’s tenure as UN Secretary-General . Sergey Lavrov stressed the importance of carefully calibrated UN reform to adapt the Organisation to the realities of a #MultipolarWorld order, ensure significantly broader representation of nationals of #GlobalMajority countries within the Secretariat, and ensure that UN staff perform their duties impartially and without favouring any side . Russia's Foreign Minister also emphasised the inadmissibility of eroding the Organisation’s intergovernmental character or disrupting the “division of labour” among its principal organs. Sergey Lavrov presented Antonio Guterres with a copy of the report “Heirs of Goebbels: Falsification of the Events in Bucha and Bloody Staged Performances of the Kiev Regime” , prepared by the International Public Tribunal led by its Chairman, member of the Civic Chamber of Russia Maxim Grigoryev . 📄 The report is devoted to exposing the false claims spread by the Kiev regime about the Bucha hoax . The Minister demanded that the UN Secretariat conduct a detailed examination of the facts surrounding the provocation staged by Kiev and its NATO sponsors . #UNGA81

🎙
Russian Foreign Ministry Spokeswoman Maria Zakharova's
statement
on the EU’s decision to impose sanctions on former RT France Editor-in-Chief Ksenia Fedorova
(September 25, 2026)
💬
On September 24,
the EU imposed sanctions
on
Ksenia Fedorova
, former Editor-in-Chief of RT France and a journalist working for French media outlets
CNews
,
Europe 1
and
JDNews
.
The EU Council justified its
illegitimate restrictions
by describing Ksenia Fedorova as
“a Russian media figure who is active in dissemination of pro-Russian narratives in France and the EU”.
There is no doubt that this latest act of political censorship and anti-Russian hysteria by Brussels, fuelled with ferocity across the West, was driven from the outset by
Paris’s desire to lend greater “legitimacy” to its recent shameful decision to expel Ksenia Fedorova from France
on equally fabricated grounds.
The journalist
, caught in the gears of repression of this
“progressive European democracy”
,
has not worked for Russian media for several years
. During that time, she has become a correspondent for several French outlets and gained popularity as a journalist and commentator on the national media scene.
☝️
Her only “offence” in the eyes of the Élysée Palace, which authorised this campaign of harassment, is that
she refused to abandon the ideals and ethics of journalism
, as the current French leadership demands, and
continued to express her views honestly
on events and developments in France and beyond.
In the imitation of democracy that France is becoming under its current leadership, this was enough
to set
the locomotive of vindictive censorship
in motion. The EU, hopelessly mired in Russophobic policies, in turn had no hesitation in endorsing this flawed logic.
The violation of Ksenia Fedorova’s legitimate professional rights –
a disgrace for the “enlightened” West and a direct breach of the international commitments
of Paris and Brussels
– once again exposes the absurdity of the “collective West’s” claims to set the standard for protecting democratic freedoms.
❗️
We call on all reasonable members of the international community to condemn this act of intimidation against honest journalism and truly independent-minded media. We demand that the relevant international bodies, including the leadership of
the Office of the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights
(OHCHR),
UNESCO
and
the OSCE
, properly assess the actions of France and the EU against their own international commitments to uphold freedom of access to information and freedom of expression.
For our part, we make clear that
the Russophobic attacks
by the countries concerned and the aggressive blocs to which they belong
will receive
an appropriate response
.

item.title: 🌍 On September 24, Russia’s Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov held a meeting with the Foreign Ministers of the Member States of
item.description: 🌍 On September 24, Russia’s Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov held a meeting with the Foreign Ministers of the Member States of the Confederation of Sahel States ( #AES ) in New York on the sidelines of the High-Level Week of the 81st Session of the UN General Assembly : 🇧🇫 Foreign Minister of #BurkinaFaso Karamoko Traore ; 🇲🇱 Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation of #Mali Abdoulaye Diop ; 🇳🇪 Minister of Foreign Affairs, Cooperation and Nigeriens Abroad of the Republic of #Niger Bakary Yaou Sangare . 👉 Sergey Lavrov's opening remarks The Sides discussed a wide range of issues in priority areas of political, economic, financial, transport, logistics and information cooperation within the Russia-AES dialogue, with a view to preparing for and holding the events of the Third Russia-Africa Summit , scheduled for October 28–29 in Moscow . They held a frank exchange of views on the situation in the Sahara-Sahel region and reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening foreign policy coordination at the UN and other international platforms . #RussiaAES

item.description: 🌏 On September 24, Russia’s Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov held his 13th meeting with high-level representatives of the Pacific Small Island Developing States in New York on the sidelines of the High-Level Week of the 81st Session of the UN General Assembly . The Sides held a substantive exchange of views on current international and regional challenges and discussed prospects for expanding bilateral cooperation between Russia and the participating countries in areas of mutual interest, including climate issues, fisheries, shipping and education. They reaffirmed their commitment to stepping up cooperation across a wide range of areas .

item.title: 🇷🇺 On September 24, Russia’s Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov and Foreign Minister of Iran Abbas Araghchi
item.description: 🇷🇺 🇮🇷 On September 24, Russia’s Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov and Foreign Minister of Iran Abbas Araghchi held a meeting in New York on the sidelines of the High-Level Week of the 81st Session of the UN General Assembly . The Sides discussed current regional and international issues, focusing on developments surrounding Iran . ❗️ They stressed that there is no alternative to a diplomatic settlement of the crisis provoked by the unlawful actions of the US and Israel . Attention was also paid to implementing the bilateral agreements reached at the meeting between the two Presidents in Bishkek on September 1, 2026. The Ministers reviewed the schedule of upcoming Russia-Iran contacts at various levels. #RussiaIran
